ONE government with THREE chambers. Macon-Bibb is the program's SECOND consolidated city-county, after Columbus/Muscogee. Stage 4 drops the county commission -- the Commission already is it -- and keeps only the separately elected county officers.

Ruling M1: NINE single-member districts and NO at-large seats. Charter Sec. 9(a) creates 'nine election districts ... Commission Districts 1 through 9'; Sec. 9(c) elects the members 'from the nine districts ... by a majority of electors voting in such election from such district'. All five GIS layers return exactly nine polygons, which is the independent confirmation. So the citywide district carries num_officials 1 -- the Mayor alone -- NOT Columbus's 3.

⚠ Ruling M1 rests on a CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE CHARTER. Sec. 5 says the commission is 'composed of a mayor and nine commissioners' and then defines every member as a 'commissioner'; Sec. 9(c) says 'The commission shall consist of nine members.' Sec. 9(c) is the provision that sets membership and voting, and it is what the body demonstrably operates under -- see the two roll calls in Ruling M2. official_count on the Commission chamber is therefore 9, not 10.

Ruling M2: the Mayor is voting_powers 'non_voting' with a required representation_note, charter Sec. 9(c): 'The mayor shall be the presiding officer of the commission but shall not be a voting member of the commission; provided, however, that the mayor may cast a vote on any matter before the commission to break a tie.' PROVED BY TWO ROLL CALLS, not asserted: the mayor pro tem was elected 5-4 among NINE in January 2025 and 5-3 among EIGHT on 2026-01-06 with District 5 vacant. Both totals are the commissioner count, never that plus one.

Ruling M3: Mayor Pro Tem is a parenthetical, not an office. Sec. 9(f): the Commission elects one of its own members annually, in January. It moved from Seth Clark to Valerie Wynn (District 1) on 2026-01-06. The post-verify gate refuses any office titled with it.

Ruling M4: 5 county officers -- Sheriff, Tax Commissioner, Coroner, Clerk of Superior Court, Judge of Probate Court. Charter Sec. 8 preserves FOUR as county officers by name; the Judge of Probate Court comes in via Ga. Const. Art. IX, Sec. I, Par. III. This is the MIRROR IMAGE of Muscogee, where the charter named the probate judge and the CLERK arrived by Art. IX. Confirmed independently: the county's own officers acted jointly as 'Bibb County constitutional officers' in December 2025 to change the county's legal organ, and Davis, Harris, Woodford and McCord are all inside that group. Bibb elects NO Marshal and NO Surveyor, so neither Baldwin's six-officer template nor Muscogee's five transfers -- the count matches Muscogee by coincidence, not by inheritance.

Ruling M5: GA-4's municipal-court question DOES NOT ARISE in Bibb. Charter Sec. 7 fills the office of judge of the Municipal Court of Macon-Bibb County 'by appointment of the mayor', so there is no elected municipal-court office to include or exclude. Confirmed by the ballot enumeration: no municipal-court contest appears in any Bibb payload. The question stays live for Philadelphia and Lexington.

Ruling M6: vacancies. Charter Sec. 15(a) orders a SPECIAL ELECTION for the balance of the unexpired term; Sec. 15(b) allows the Commission to APPOINT within 20 days if the vacancy falls within 12 months of the term's expiry. This is what makes how_started differ seat by seat, and it is load-bearing: Bailey and Stewart are 'appointed', Wynn and Cooke won specials.

how_started 'special election' IS NOT A LEGAL VALUE. essentials.office_terms carries CHECK how_started IN ('elected','appointed','succeeded','redistricted','unknown'). Wynn and Cooke won SPECIAL elections, so how_started is 'elected' and the special-election fact is carried in the source string and the migration header, not in the column. This is the GA-4 Task 3 correction, restated so it cannot be lost when the roster is edited.

⚠ TWO PRESS ACCOUNTS SAY THE MAYOR APPOINTED BAILEY TO DISTRICT 9. Charter Sec. 15(b) gives that power to 'the commission or those remaining', and the reported tally was a 5-3 COMMISSION vote with Lucas, Bronson and Watkins opposed. how_started is 'appointed' either way, but the source string must not repeat the error.

⚠ term_start IS CONTINUOUS OCCUPANCY, NOT THE CURRENT TERM. The county published 'The four-year term of office for each of these officials begins at 12:00 a.m. on January 1, 2025' and listed all ten. That date is correct ONLY for Hulett and Bryant. Seven others were already serving, two of them seated mid-2024 by appointment, and one since 2018. Taking the published sentence at face value would have back-dated three people and forward-dated five.

⚠ THE OATH IS THE OCCUPANCY, NOT THE VOTE. WGXA headlines Stewart 'sworn in early' on 2024-10-01, the day the Commission voted to appoint him; the county's own post reports the oath on Tuesday 2024-10-15, with his first Commission meeting that evening. And one outlet dates Cooke's oath to April 21 2026, a TUESDAY, while the article says 'sworn in Monday' and 'first commission meeting is Tuesday' -- so 2026-04-20. The weekday arbitrates.

⚠ RULING RECORDED 2026-09-01 (Cantrell): the four rows that begin 2021-01-01 are written at start_precision 'day', with the derivation in the source string and never as a quotation. No source quotes the date. It is the charter's own commencement rule -- Sec. 9(c) and Sec. 10(b), 'shall take office on the first day of January immediately following the date of the election' -- applied to a sourced 2020 election, and the county states that identical rule as fact for the 2025 cohort. This is a legal rule applied to a sourced election, NOT the GA-4 Chapple case, where a date inferred from vague prose was correctly refused and written 'unknown'.

⚠ WYNN IS 'month' DELIBERATELY. Gary Bechtel resigned District 1 to run for the state House; the special election was 2018-05-22 and the runoff 2018-06-19, which she won 677-582. No source examined states the oath date, so the day is not written.

⚠ WOODFORD, McCORD AND JONES ARE OPEN-ENDED 'unknown' DELIBERATELY. All three are confirmed in office, but no source examined states when their occupancy began. Coroner Jones has 'been elected six times' with a term ending 2028, which would arithmetically place him in office from 2005 -- that is arithmetic on a press phrase, not a source, and it is not written. Columbus wrote nine of eleven this way.

Party is deliberately absent. It lives on races.primary_party, never on a person or an office. ⚠ The county's voter-facing GIS layer carries a party1 field reading 'Non-Partisan' for all nine; it is not read.

🔴 'Macon County' is NOT Macon's county. Production holds both 13021 Bibb County, which contains the city of Macon, and 13193 Macon County, a rural county some 60 miles away. Bibb is the parent. 13193 is carried as a standing negative control in the boundary loader.

chambers.name: Macon-Bibb County Commission
chambers.rationale: official_count is 9, not 10. Charter Sec. 9(c): 'The commission shall consist of nine members.' The Mayor is elected separately and is not one of the nine -- Sec. 9(c) makes him the presiding officer and expressly not a voting member. ⚠ Sec. 5 describes the body as 'a mayor and nine commissioners', which contradicts this; Sec. 9(c) governs, and the two mayor pro tem roll calls (5-4 of nine, then 5-3 of eight with a seat vacant) show which one the body follows.

offices.title: Mayor
offices.representation_note: The Mayor of Macon-Bibb County is elected countywide and presides over the nine-member Macon-Bibb County Commission. Under Section 9(c) of the Charter of Macon-Bibb County, the Mayor is the presiding officer of the Commission but is not a voting member of it, and may cast a vote on a matter before the Commission only to break a tie. The Mayor may propose ordinances in the same manner as a commissioner. Macon-Bibb County is a strong-mayor government, so the Mayor is also its chief executive, responsible for carrying out its laws and policies. If the office of Mayor becomes vacant, Section 15(c) makes the mayor pro tempore the acting mayor.
